battle.name: 第四次阿散蒂戰爭
battle.theater: 黃金海岸至庫馬西走廊
battle.brief: 一八九四年一月，英軍遠征軍沿新鋪嘅公路直逼阿散蒂王都庫馬西，破城而入並將全城縱火焚燒，四月追入北方擒獲阿散蒂王科菲・卡里卡里，黃金凳亦落入英方手中。呢場仗全喺內陸打，鐵甲艦冇到過西非；但英方退到射程之外用砲火壓制、唔碰城牆嘅做法，正正就係鐵甲艦年代落低嚟嘅戰爭邏輯。

kit.name: 鐵甲艦
kit.history: 木殼外面包了鐵。裝甲第一次比砲更難對付，砲塔的設計從此繞著它轉。

countries: 英方係大不列顛帝國喺黃金海岸殖民地拉出嚟嘅遠征軍，唔係常備師團，而係由殖民地總督麥卡錫坐鎮開普海岸、遠征司令同海軍分隊長喺前線分權指揮嘅一支臨時力量。地面有皇家陸軍步兵連隊同皇家工兵，工兵專責鋪路、築壘、架橋、拉電報線；海上由皇家海軍西非分遣隊運兵、運糧、運砲，維持開普海岸到阿散蒂邊境嘅航道，並攔截運入內陸嘅軍火。殖民地嗰邊有皇家西非邊防軍，以北方招嚟嘅豪薩兵為骨幹，再加上海岸族群提供嘅民兵同擔夫，負責護路、徵糧同外圍巡邏。英軍嘅指揮靠職級、軍令同電報線，命令落得又快又齊；阿散蒂方完全唔同：阿散蒂王國以阿散蒂王為中心，首都庫馬西，國土分做幾十個省，每省由首長帶領自己嘅民兵，兵員臨時徵召，武器係自家鑄嘅小砲同前膛火槍，糧食靠周邊農村同衛星城支應。中央議事會可以議決大事，但命令傳到各村要靠口耳同信差，行軍速度遠慢過英軍。
countriesEn: The British side was not a standing army but an expeditionary force raised in the Gold Coast colony of the British Empire: Governor MacCarthy based himself at Cape Coast while an expedition commander and a naval detachment commander shared the command in the field. On land the force included companies of Royal Army infantry and the Royal Engineers, whose job was road building, stockades, bridge construction and the telegraph line; at sea the Royal Navy's West African detachment carried troops, food and guns, kept the coastal channel open between Cape Coast and the Ashanti frontier, and stopped arms from slipping inland. The colonial side provided the Royal West African Frontier Force, whose backbone was Hausa soldiers recruited in the Northern Territories, together with coastal militia and porters who escorted convoys, requisitioned food and patrolled the flanks. British command ran on rank, written orders and the telegraph, so orders arrived quickly and together; the Ashanti system was nothing like it. The Asante state was centred on the Asantehene at Kumasi, divided into dozens of provinces, each led by its own chief with his own levy, raised on the spot, armed with home-cast small guns and muzzleloaders and fed from the villages and satellite towns around them. A central council could decide great matters, but word to the villages travelled by mouth and runner, so the army moved far more slowly than the British.
people: 殖民地總督麥卡錫係今場戰爭嘅政治發起人：佢喺一八九二年派羅伯特・霍奇森帶住公函同禮物入庫馬西交涉，攞唔到黃金凳，英方就喺佢手上決定用兵，倫敦嘅殖民地大臣張伯倫亦支持向前推進。皇家海軍嘅史考夫中將率海軍分遣隊上岸作戰，之後接手突擊縱隊，喺一八九四年一月十七日帶隊入庫馬西並縱火焚城，戰後受封爵士。阿散蒂方面嘅阿散蒂王科菲・卡里卡里自一八八八年繼位，面對交出黃金凳同讓英方修路築站兩項要求都唔肯低頭；城破之後佢北走，到同年四月在北方領地被人捉住，押上船送去塞拉利昂流放，最後病逝喺流亡地。守住黃金凳嘅司職祭司同幾名侍從被英軍俘獲，供出聖凳嘅藏處。值得留意嘅係，阿散蒂軍冇一位能號令全軍嘅大將，各省首長各帶各嘅人馬，海軍分遣隊同皇家陸軍之間亦靠總督同參謀長協調，而唔係由一個人話事。
peopleEn: Governor MacCarthy was the political author of the war: in 1892 he sent Hodgson into Kumasi with a letter and gifts, came back without the Golden Stool, and on MacCarthy's advice the decision was taken to use force, with the Colonial Secretary in London supporting the forward policy. Rear-Admiral Francis Scott brought the naval brigade ashore, then took over a flying column and entered Kumasi with his men on 17 January 1894, putting the city to the torch; he was knighted for it afterwards. On the Ashanti side the Asantehene Kofi Karikari, who had succeeded in 1888, refused both British demands, surrendering the stool and accepting a British road and station. After the city fell he fled north, was taken in the northern territories in April of the same year and shipped into exile in Sierra Leone, where he later died. The priestly custodian of the Golden Stool and his attendants were captured and gave up the hiding place. One point deserves emphasis: the Ashanti army had no single commander able to order the whole force; each provincial chief led his own men, and even between the naval brigade and the army units coordination ran through the Governor and his staff rather than through one man.
kits: 卡面呢件兵器係一八六二年嘅英國鐵甲艦：木殼外面包鐵，裝甲第一次比砲更難對付，砲塔設計亦由呢度改寫。不過要老老實實講清楚：呢艘鐵甲艦從來冇到過西非海岸，更加冇參與過一八九四年嘅戰鬥。一八六二年嘅英國主力鐵甲艦係為遠洋部署而造，任務喺北極、地中海同遠東；到一八九○年代中葉，側舷鐵甲艦已經全部拆解，連最後幾艘都喺一八八○年代末賣咗俾拆船廠，黃金海岸分遣隊上嘅船係木殼同複合殼嘅砲艦、汽艇同巡洋艦，一艘都冇裝甲。但鐵甲艦年代教落嚟嘅習慣，就係呢場戰爭嘅骨架：唔撞，而係退到射程之外用火炮一點點打。英軍面對庫馬西嘅土牆木柵，用嘅正正係同一個辦法——皇家砲兵嘅七磅、九磅野戰砲同海軍分遣隊帶上岸嘅十二磅、六磅快射砲，喺城牆外反覆轟擊，唔派突擊隊去撞牆。步兵主力用一八八八年列裝嘅馬提尼・亨利式後膛槍，口徑約〇・五七七英吋；殖民地部隊同豪薩兵用〇・五零至〇・七零口徑嘅史賓塞同陷阱式後膛槍；阿散蒂軍用〇・六九口徑滑膛前膛火槍，另有數十門自鑄小砲，口徑細、射程短、彈藥自製，配刀、矛、盾同藤甲。馬克沁機關槍喺呢個年代已經入列，但數量極少，喺戰場上只可以見到零星小組。工兵帶住測量工具同工程器材，喺路上築起一連串土牆木柵嘅據點，等於將海上嘅砲艦原封搬上陸地，變成固定嘅射擊陣地，唔怕人燒。糧食彈藥靠牛車、騡隊同人力擔夫沿新路運入，內陸路段同雨季令呢條補給線成為遠征軍最大嘅弱點。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is a British ironclad of 1862: a wooden shell sheathed in iron, the first time armour proved harder to deal with than guns, and turret design was rewritten from that point on. It has to be said plainly, however, that this ironclad never reached West Africa and took no part in the fighting of 1894. The British capital ironclads of 1862 were built for distant-station service, in the Arctic, the Mediterranean and the Far East; by the mid-1890s the broadside ironclad had gone entirely, the last of them sold for breaking up in the late 1880s, and the ships on the West African station were wooden or composite gunboats, sloops and cruisers, none of them carrying armour. Yet the habit the ironclad era left behind is the skeleton of this war: do not ram, stand off at range and pound. Facing the earthwork and stockade of Kumasi, the British used exactly that method, the Royal Artillery's 7-pounder and 9-pounder field guns together with the 12-pounder and 6-pounder quick-firers landed by the naval brigade, working over the walls again and again, and they did not send infantry to butt their heads against the rampart. British infantry carried the Martini-Henry breech-loader, standardised in 1888, of about 0.577 inch calibre; colonial troops and the Hausa used Springfield and Trapdoor breech-loaders of 0.50 to 0.70 inch; the Ashanti had 0.69 inch smoothbore muzzleloaders and a few dozen home-cast pieces with small bore, short range and home-made ammunition, with knives, spears, shields and rattan armour. The Maxim machine gun was in service by this period, but in tiny numbers, and only a handful of sections could be seen in the field. The sappers carried survey and engineering stores and built a chain of earth-and-timber posts along the road, which was a gun platform lifted ashore unchanged, a fixed battery no one could burn. Food and ammunition came up the new road in bullock carts, mule trains and on men's backs, and the interior stages, together with the rains, made that line of supply the expedition's weakest point.
tactics: 英軍唔會同阿散蒂比人數，佢用三樣嘢換取勝利：路、砲同速度。工程兵先喺前鋒位置一日日把路向前鋪，每一段路嘅盡頭築起據點，電報線跟住路一齊伸過去，於是後方可以逐日向前移；主力唔會一次過壓上，而係組成縱隊，由縱隊首長帶住幾百人快速推進，唔同阿散蒂主力正面撞，只係守住路、逼近城牆。真正嘅攻擊之前，皇家砲兵同海軍分遣隊先做炮火準備——七磅、九磅野戰砲同十二磅快射砲喺城牆外反覆轟擊土牆同木柵，等缺口打開，先由步兵散開佔領缺口，再逐間屋推進。入城之後就縱火，一八九四年一月十七日由南面貝克瓦伊方向攻入，控制全城大約用咗一個星期。阿散蒂方面嘅打法完全相反：守城部隊以土牆、木柵、門樓同土築碉堡構成，士兵唔排密集隊形，而係散開喺林頭、田埂同屋頂，進行零散射擊，令英軍唔敢行得太快；游擊隊專門切英軍嘅糧道、徵糧隊同前哨，用土牆同倒樹封死道路，逼英軍逐段清理；主力則集中喺庫馬西周邊同北方幾條路上，想用守城同拉長戰線拖住英軍。哈麥丹乾風吹到嘅日子，沙塵會令視線縮到幾百碼，砲手只可以靠方向同砲聲判斷敵陣位置。
tacticsEn: The British did not try to outnumber the Ashanti; they traded on three things, the road, the guns and speed. Sappers pushed the road forward day by day, ending each stretch with a post, and the telegraph followed the road, so the rear could creep forward behind it. The main body was not committed in one mass but formed into flying columns, a few hundred men under a column leader moving fast, never colliding head-on with the Ashanti main force, simply holding the road and closing on the walls. Before the real attack the Royal Artillery and the naval brigade prepared the ground, the 7-pounder and 9-pounder field guns and the 12-pounders pounding the earth walls and stockades until a breach opened, and only then did the infantry spread out to take it and work forward house by house. Once inside, they fired the city. The entry on 17 January 1894 came from the south by the Bekwai road, and the city was under British control within about a week. The Ashanti method was the mirror image: the garrison held earth walls, timber palisades, gate towers and mud blockhouses, and instead of standing in close formation the men dispersed among the tree lines, the ridges and the rooftops, firing in small groups so that the British could not hurry. Raiding parties went after the baggage, the food convoys and the outposts, blocking the road with earth banks and felled trees so that the British had to clear it stage by stage, while the main body was concentrated around Kumasi and along the northern tracks, hoping to wear the campaign out by holding the city and stretching the line. When the harmattan blew, the dust cut visibility to a few hundred yards and the gunners could only judge the enemy's position by compass bearing and by the sound of the guns.
data: 時間線好清楚：衝突喺一八九三年下半年就喺沿海公路上打開，一八九四年一月十七日英軍攻入庫馬西並焚城，四月科菲・卡里卡里被俘，同年四月底戰事大致結束。規模上，英方遠征軍連同殖民地部隊有數千人，包括海軍陸戰隊、皇家陸軍步兵連隊、皇家工兵、皇家砲兵同豪薩兵；按當時嘅估計，阿散蒂方面可以召集嘅民兵以萬計，但多數只帶前膛火槍同土製彈藥，訓練同補給都差啲。距離方面，由開普海岸到庫馬西嘅公路約一百五十至二百公里，中途要過安科布拉河同奧芬河，電報線同路一齊鋪設，命令由海岸送到前線只需一日。火砲方面，英軍有七磅同九磅野戰砲、海軍十二磅同六磅快射砲，砲兵營另外配少量大口徑攻城砲；阿散蒂一方只有數十門自鑄小砲，口徑只有幾吋，射程短、精度低。城防方面，庫馬西係土石加木柵砌成嘅城牆，門口用石頭同木材堵死，城內有幾座土築碉堡。損失方面，英軍陣亡人數以百計，受傷者多過陣亡，死於阿散蒂舊式前膛火槍者佔多數，因為阿散蒂兵要行到近距離先開火；非歐洲士兵因為瘧疾、勞損同食糧變質嘅非戰減員，反而多過陣亡人數。
dataEn: The chronology is clear: the fighting opened on the coastal road in the second half of 1893, the British entered and burned Kumasi on 17 January 1894, Karikari was captured in April, and the campaign was essentially over by the end of that April. On numbers, the expeditionary force with its colonial contingents numbered several thousand men, including the naval brigade, companies of Royal Army infantry, the Royal Engineers, the Royal Artillery and the Hausa; on the Ashanti side the levies that could be mustered ran into tens of thousands, but most carried only muzzleloaders and home-made ammunition and were short of training and supply. As for distance, the road from Cape Coast to Kumasi ran something like 150 to 200 kilometres, crossing the Ankobra and the Offin, with the telegraph laid alongside it so that an order from the coast took a day to reach the front. In artillery terms the British fielded 7-pounder and 9-pounder guns and the navy's 12-pounder and 6-pounder quick-firers, with a few heavy pieces in the siege park; the Asante had only a few dozen home-cast guns of a few inches bore, short-ranged and inaccurate. The defences of Kumasi were earth and timber walls with the gateways blocked by stone and wood, and there were several mud blockhouses inside the town. On losses, British dead numbered in the hundreds with more wounded than killed, and most of those deaths came from old muzzleloaders fired at close range; among non-European soldiers, sickness, hard labour and spoiled rations took away more men by disease than the enemy did in battle.
cause: 背景係一八七四年英軍攻佔庫馬西之後：阿散蒂王國名義上臣服，實際上靠叢林深處嘅黃金凳保住象徵主權——阿散蒂人相信凳就係國家同王室嘅靈魂，交出凳等於交出國家。英方一直想攞返凳作為臣服嘅證明，同時要修一條由開普海岸通庫馬西嘅公路，好做貿易、治安同行政，仲要喺庫馬西駐紮人手管住新路。一八九二年總督麥卡錫派霍奇森入城交涉，結果凳冇到手，路亦開唔成，霍奇森返嚟就主張用兵。阿散蒂方嘅反應係關咗庫馬西市場、唔同英國人做生意、襲擊路上嘅商隊同徵糧隊。沿海族群同阿散蒂嘅世仇亦畀咗英方介入嘅理由。加上當時英國喺非洲全面向前推進、由殖民地大臣張伯倫主導嘅政策氣氛，一八九四年一月英軍向庫馬西推進，衝突就咁全面爆發。
causeEn: The background was the British occupation of Kumasi in 1874. The Asante state submitted in name but kept symbolic sovereignty in the Golden Stool hidden in the forest, because the Asante held that the stool was the soul of the state and of its royal line, and to give it up was to give up the country. The British wanted the stool back as proof of submission, and they wanted a road from Cape Coast to Kumasi for trade, for pacification and for administration, with a British station at Kumasi to police the new route. When MacCarthy sent Hodgson into the capital in 1892 to negotiate, the stool was not forthcoming and the road could not be built, and Hodgson came back advocating force. The Asante answered by closing the Kumasi market, refusing to trade with the British and raiding the convoys and food parties on the road. The old feuds between the coastal clans and the Asante gave the British a further reason to step in. Added to that was the whole forward policy in Africa under the Colonial Secretary in London, and when British columns moved on Kumasi in January 1894 the conflict opened in full.
impact: 對阿散蒂王國嚟講，呢場仗係致命嘅：庫馬西變成焦炭，王室成員被俘或者流放，黃金凳被運去英國，王國從此唔再係一個有實力嘅政體，而係英國殖民地裡面一個被拆散嘅聯邦——各省首長嘅權力被削走，英國派駐節常駐，於是阿散蒂嘅問題冇解決，只係換咗個形式繼續存在。黃金凳呢件事更加拖得長：英方一直唔肯交返，雖然一九○○年嘅邦德協議准阿散蒂喺北方監管下保管聖凳，但唔准帶回庫馬西；凳子要到一九五七年先由英方送返加納，一九九二年先由阿散蒂王攜返庫馬西。英方本身亦付出代價：遠征軍喺瘧疾、糧食同交通上消耗大量金錢，而殖民地財政長期入不敷出，呢啲數字後來成為英國檢討非洲政策嘅重要依據。戰術上，呢場仗證明咗「路加電報加縱隊加砲火」喺非洲內陸行得通，之後二十年間英國喺撒哈拉以南非洲嘅軍事行動，好多都係照呢個樣板做。對西非其他國家嚟講，效果更震撼：一個唔大嘅內陸王國只要守住象徵同森林，英國照樣會派遠征軍嚟——呢個訊息令唔少族群相信抵抗係有可能，亦令英國知道每一次遠征都要付出遠高於預期嘅代價。
impactEn: For the Asante state the war was ruinous. Kumasi was a burnt shell, members of the royal house were taken or exiled, the Golden Stool was carried off to England, and from then on the Asante were no longer a power but a federation broken up inside a British colony, their chiefs stripped of authority and a British Resident permanently resident among them, so the Asante question was not solved, only changed shape. The business of the stool dragged on for decades: London would not give it back, and although the Bond of 1900 allowed the Asante to keep the stool under supervision in the north, it could not be brought to Kumasi; it went back to Ghana in 1957 and was only carried back to Kumasi by the Asantehene in 1992. Britain paid too. The expedition drained money through fever, food and transport, and the colony's finances were permanently in deficit, figures that later counted in the British reappraisal of African policy. Tactically the war proved that road, telegraph, flying column and artillery could be made to work in the African interior, and much of what Britain did in sub-Saharan Africa over the next twenty years was done to that pattern. The effect on other West African states was even more striking: an inland kingdom of no great size, holding on to its symbol and its forest, could still bring a British expedition across the country, and that told other peoples that resistance was possible while telling Britain that every expedition cost far more than had been budgeted.

resultEn: On 17 January 1894 the British column entered Kumasi and the city was burned, and British control was complete within days. The Asantehene Kofi Karikari fled north, was captured in April and taken by ship into exile in Sierra Leone, where he died. The Golden Stool fell into British hands with its custodian, the single block of hardwood carved and then gilded, and was later shipped back to England. The settlement required the Asante to accept a British Resident, to open their markets, to pull down part of the walls and works and to pay for the war; in this way, dismantling the city and quartering troops on it, Kumasi became a British-held post. Tactically the result was a British win: the road was open, the telegraph was laid, the Ashanti defences and army were broken and the stool was taken. Politically it was thin. The Asante refused to accept the outcome, and in 1895 and 1896 they rose again to bring the stool back by force, so the British had to enter Kumasi a second time and take Prempeh, the heir, away to Sierra Leone as well; it took the Bond of 1900 to settle the stool's whereabouts even temporarily. That outcome carries the lesson of the 1862 ironclad: the age of armour was over, but the business of keeping influence at a distance by technology, engineering and projection is exactly why Britain won the battle in the Gold Coast and did not win the peace.
